meta.subtitle: Fabless power-management supplier growing on AI demand, priced for a ramp that leaves little margin for a stall

analystSentiment.commentary: We rate Monolithic Power Systems a HOLD with a target range of $1,300 to $1,700 against a current price of $1,351.20. Our probability-weighted fair value is $1,484.54, an expected upside of 9.9%, with a bear-case downside of 28.9% and a reward/risk of 0.34x, well short of the 0.50x a BUY needs. The business is performing: Q2'26 revenue of $980.6 million rose 47.6% year over year and operating margin reached 31.0%. The price already asks a great deal of it. Our Base assumes the current-year multiple eases as growth slows into FY27E, and our Bear prices an earnings stall of the kind the company's own income statement has shown before. We sit below the $1,839.80 consensus target because we do not assume the multiple expands. The call is close: if the market keeps paying today's current-year multiple a year from now, the same scenarios derive BUY, and the valuation section argues that split from both sides.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Monolithic Power Systems is a fabless supplier of semiconductor-based power electronics, founded in 1997 by its CEO Michael Hsing and based in West Palm Beach, Florida. Its DC-to-DC and AC-to-DC solutions, driver metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors and power management integrated circuits convert and control voltage in servers, AI systems, memory, storage, vehicles, network infrastructure, appliances and other electronics. Third parties manufacture, assemble and test its ICs, so the company spends its own resources on design. It sells through third-party distributors, value-added resellers and direct customers. FY25 revenue was $2.8 billion, up 26.4%. The company reports a single segment and breaks revenue out across six end markets: enterprise data, storage and computing, automotive, communications, consumer and industrial.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: The case for owning MPWR is power content in AI and data-center systems. Enterprise data led Q2'26 revenue growth of 47.6%, on higher sales of power management solutions for AI and server applications, and operating margin widened to 31.0% from 24.8% a year earlier. The case for waiting is price: the shares trade at 49.3x current-year consensus EPS, and the income statement shows that a surge in growth has been followed by a flat year before. Weighing both, the scenarios derive HOLD, because an expected upside of 9.9% does not compensate for a Bear 28.9% below the price. The label turns on whether the current-year multiple compresses as growth slows, and we judge that more likely than not.

catalysts: Enterprise data: AI and server power demand drove the Q2'26 growth; another quarter at that pace would support the Bull case.
Communications: power solutions for optical modules and switches lifted this end market in Q2'26, a second data-infrastructure source of growth.
Consensus delivery: FY26E revenue of about $4.1 billion and FY27E of $5.3 billion, if met, support the Base.
Capital return: the February 2026 dividend increase, covered under capital allocation.
risks: Valuation: the multiples discussed under valuation leave little room for a growth miss.
Concentration: most revenue comes from customers in Asia and from a limited number of customers, as set out under Risks.
Internal control: the material weakness and FY24 restatement discussed under governance.
Cyclicality: customers can cancel or reschedule orders without significant penalty, and the company calls its industry cyclical.
Cash conversion: FY25 free cash flow converted less of revenue than in FY23 or FY24, as the cash-flow section shows.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: Q2'26 revenue was $980.6 million, up 47.6% from $664.6 million in Q2'25, and first-half revenue of $1,784.8 million rose 37.1% year over year. The company attributes the increase primarily to demand in its enterprise data and communications end markets, with a higher product mix of power solutions, which generally carry higher average selling prices than discrete ICs, also contributing. Gross margin was 55.2% in Q2'26 against 55.1% a year earlier, so the margin gain came from operating expenses: research and development fell to 12.1% of revenue from 14.5%, and selling, general and administrative to 12.1% from 15.8%, taking operating margin to 31.0% from 24.8%. FY25 GAAP net income was $621.5 million, or $12.86 per diluted share, against FY24's $1,592.1 million and $32.60, figures the company restated in February 2026. The proxy attributes the decline primarily to a ten-year tax incentive granted to a foreign subsidiary in 2024, for which a deferred tax benefit of approximately $1.1 billion was recorded in 2024. The proxy also reports FY25 non-GAAP diluted EPS of $17.77. The page does not say whether consensus EPS is on a GAAP or non-GAAP basis, so we do not measure the step-up to FY26E against either FY25 figure.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: FY25 cash and short-term investments were about $1.0 billion and total equity was $3.1 billion, up from $1.2 billion in FY21. The Facts block shows no total-debt or net-debt figure for any year, and the trailing net debt/EBITDA and interest coverage cells are blank, so we treat leverage as not reported rather than as zero and do not call the company debt-free. The current ratio was 4.92 at FY25 and 4.98 on a trailing basis. The FY25 reading is the lowest of the five years shown, down from 7.74 in FY23, but current assets still cover current liabilities several times over. On these figures, liquidity does not constrain the dividend or the business.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Operating cash flow rounds to $0.8 billion in both FY24 and FY25 in the table, even though FY25 revenue rose 26.4%. FY25 capital expenditure was $174.9 million, and free cash flow was $663.3 million, a 23.8% margin. That margin is below the 31.9% of FY23 and the 28.3% of FY24, so cash conversion has lagged revenue growth for two years. The pack does not explain the gap, and we do not assign a cause; the next annual cash-flow statement will show whether it persists at higher revenue. Capital expenditure stays small against revenue, as a fabless model should, at $0.2 billion in each of FY24 and FY25. The trailing free-cash-flow yield of 0.9% is low, and that reflects the share price more than the cash flow.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: The shares trade at 82.5x trailing earnings, 20.3x sales and 65.4x trailing EV/EBITDA. The page labels 49.3x a next-twelve-months P/E, but it lines up with the FY26E consensus EPS of $27.43, so we treat it as today's current-year multiple; on FY27E EPS of $34.87 the shares trade at 38.7x. No peer multiples were captured and the pack carries no history of the stock's own multiple, so the other reference is the Street: a $1,839.80 consensus target and $1,820.00 median, in a $1,575.00 to $2,100.00 range across 17 analysts, 16 of them at Buy. The price of $1,351.20 sits below the $1,714.09 52-week high and well above the $833.18 low; no source in the pack explains the move from the high. The valuation question is which current-year multiple the market will pay a year from now, when FY27 is the current year.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Enterprise-data and communications demand keeps growth near the Q2'26 pace, FY27E EPS of $34.87 is met or beaten, operating margin holds near the Q2'26 level of 31.0%, and a year out the market pays somewhat more than today's current-year multiple. We anchor the Bull to the $1,839.80 consensus target rather than the $2,100.00 Street high, which would need a larger re-rating.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Growth slows from the FY26E pace of about 48% toward the FY27E consensus of $5.3 billion in revenue, FY27E consensus EPS is met, and the current-year multiple eases from today's 49.3x to 45x, our assumption for a business still growing but more slowly than in FY26.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: AI capacity digestion or a semiconductor downturn stalls earnings, so FY27 EPS stays near the FY26E consensus of $27.43, and the multiple falls to 35x. That multiple is our assumption, set below the 38.7x the market pays today for FY27E growth that, in this scenario, does not arrive. The $833.18 52-week low marks a deeper outcome we treat as a tail.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: Weighting the Bull at 25%, the Base at 50% and the Bear at 25% gives a fair value of $1,484.54, an expected upside of 9.9%, a bear-case downside of 28.9% and a reward/risk of 0.34x, which derives HOLD. Two assumptions decide it. The first is the Base multiple. If the market still pays today's current-year multiple a year out, these scenarios derive BUY; if it pays only what it pays today for FY27E, the Base equals today's price. For holding the multiple: Q2'26 margins, enterprise-data momentum and a Street almost entirely at Buy. For compression: consensus has revenue growth slowing from FY26E to FY27E, the trailing multiple shows how much the price already anticipates, and we expect the market to pay less for slower growth. We take the middle path in the Base and call the split close; the label rests on it. The second is the Bear weight. For a lower weight: the Q2'26 operating margin and the company's statement that no trade restriction had a material impact through the 10-Q filing date. For a higher one: the income statement shows revenue growth of 48.5% in FY22 followed by 1.5% in FY23, when diluted EPS slipped to $8.76 from $9.05, and FY26E consensus has growth near 48% again. We keep the Bear weight equal to the Bull's because the pack offers no evidence that tilts the odds either way.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Monolithic Power Systems reports a single segment and breaks revenue out by end market in the 10-Q. In Q2'26, enterprise data was 38.8% of revenue, up from 21.7% a year earlier, after growing 164.3%, which the company attributes primarily to higher sales of power management solutions for AI and server applications. Communications, at 13.4%, grew 78.3% on power solutions for optical modules and switches. Storage and computing, which at 29.4% of Q2'25 revenue was then ahead of enterprise data, was 20.4% after growing 2.3%. Automotive was 16.0% after growing 8.2% on applications supporting infotainment and lighting systems; consumer was 5.8% after falling 4.8%; industrial was 5.6% after growing 17.3%. Six end markets give the single segment some breadth, but the growth now comes mostly from two data-infrastructure markets.

moatFactors.name: Design and system integration
moatFactors.body: The company names three core strengths: deep system-level knowledge, strong semiconductor design expertise, and proprietary technologies in semiconductor processes, system integration and packaging. Gross margin stayed between 55.2% and 58.4% in each year from FY21 to FY25, including FY23's flat year. The limit is that a design position does not lock in volume, given the order terms set out under Risks.

moatFactors.name: Fabless capital efficiency
moatFactors.body: Working with third parties to manufacture, assemble and test its ICs has, in the company's words, enabled it to limit capital expenditures and fixed costs. The cash-flow table bears that out, with capital expenditure small against revenue in every year shown.

moatFactors.name: Customer and geographic concentration
moatFactors.body: Most revenue comes from customers in Asia, and the 10-K cites dependence on a limited number of customers, as detailed under Risks. A concentrated demand base narrows the moat, because a few buyers or one region's trade conditions can move results.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat narrow. Design capability and a capital-light model have produced the growth record noted under management and a gross margin that stayed in the range shown above in every year. Against that, the 10-K names competition from companies with greater financial and technological resources and from customers developing products internally, and customers can cancel or reschedule orders without significant penalty. Today's growth comes mostly from enterprise data and communications, so durability depends on other end markets carrying growth if AI demand digests.

points: Consensus revenue of about $4.1 billion for FY26E, about 48% growth, and $5.3 billion for FY27E, against FY25's $2.8 billion.
Capacity: the 2026 proxy says the company secured more than $4 billion of geographically balanced capacity in 2025 and continues to add supply chain partners to support future growth.

Automotive: the proxy describes 2025 launches for 48V and zonal architectures, including what it calls the first fully integrated 48V e-fuse and a kilowatt level zonal controller, which it says will support growth in 2026 and beyond. Q2'26 automotive revenue grew more slowly than the company total.
Data center: the proxy reports an expanded customer base for power solutions across AI, server, memory, optical module and switch applications, and sampling of an 800V power solution for data center.

Breadth: the proxy says non-Enterprise Data end markets grew by over 40% year over year in 2025; in Q2'26, growth outside enterprise data and communications was slower, as the end-market detail shows.

management.leadership: Michael Hsing, who founded the company in 1997, is Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer. The other named executive officers for 2025 in the 2026 proxy are Bernie Blegen, Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer; Deming Xiao, Executive Vice President, Global Operations; Maurice Sciammas, Executive Vice President, Worldwide Sales and Marketing; and Saria Tseng, Executive Vice President, Strategic Corporate Development, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary. The proxy says the Compensation Committee has focused executives on accountability in revenue, operating income and earnings. On delivery, the proxy reports a 14th consecutive year of revenue growth in 2025; the material weakness discussed under governance is the main mark against execution.
management.capitalAllocation: The Board raised the quarterly dividend 28% to $2.00 per share, or $8.00 annually, in February 2026, after declaring $6.24 per share for FY25. Repurchases have been uneven: $0.6 billion in FY24 and $6.6 million in FY25, when dividends paid were $284.8 million. The 2026 proxy says the company returned 72% of free cash flows to stockholders through dividends and repurchases over the past three years. We see the dividend as the main channel of return; whether repurchases resume at FY24's scale depends partly on whether cash conversion recovers.
management.governance: The 2026 proxy, filed April 30, 2026, reports that the Board has determined six of its seven directors are independent under NASDAQ listing standards: Herbert Chang, Eugen Elmiger, Victor K. Lee, Carintia Martinez, Eileen Wynne and Jeff Zhou. Michael Hsing is both Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. The larger issue is internal control. The FY25 10-K lists risks tied to the identified material weakness and the restatement of prior financial statements, the proxy says FY24 GAAP net income and diluted EPS were restated in February 2026, and the June-quarter 10-Q still lists remediating the material weakness among its forward-looking matters. The proxy says the restatement did not affect the other measures in its summary table, including revenue and operating income. Until remediation is reported, we treat the risk of further adjustments as open.
management.insiderOwnership: As of the 2026 proxy's Record Date, Michael Hsing beneficially owned 1,034,099 shares, or 2.1%, and all current executive officers and directors as a group held 1,786,772 shares, or 3.6%, based on 49,129,267 shares outstanding. The 5% holders listed are The Vanguard Group at 12.1%, BlackRock, Inc. at 10.0% and FMR LLC at 8.1%. Insider ownership is modest, so outside holders rely on the board and pay design rather than on a controlling founder stake to align management with them.

idiosyncratic: Concentration: 92% of FY25 revenue came from customers in Asia, per the 10-K, and sales to direct customers in Asia were 94% of Q2'26 revenue, per the 10-Q. The 10-K also cites dependence on a limited number of customers. Its risk summary ties this to China's economy and regulation, U.S.-China trade policy, the Renminbi, and political risk in Taiwan and Hong Kong.
Single driver: the Q2'26 expansion came mostly from enterprise data, as the end-market detail shows, so a pause in AI and server demand would hit results harder than the six-market spread suggests.

Forecasting: customers can cancel or reschedule orders without significant penalty, supply chain lead times generally run 16 to 26 weeks, and a new product takes a number of quarters to ramp, which the company says makes orders, revenue and expenses difficult to forecast.
Valuation: at the current-year multiple discussed under valuation, a modest growth miss could move the shares more than it would a lower-multiple stock.
risks.systemic: The company describes the semiconductor industry as cyclical and names the macroeconomic pressures on it: consumer spending, semiconductor demand, inflation, global tariffs and retaliatory measures, interest rates and currency. On trade, the 10-Q says no export-control or tariff restriction had a material impact on revenue and operations in the June quarter or through its filing date, but that such restrictions can be enacted quickly and unexpectedly and could impact the business. A broad downturn in electronics demand or a U.S.-China escalation could pressure revenue and the multiple at the same time, which is the outcome the Bear prices.

body: We rate Monolithic Power Systems a HOLD with a $1,300 to $1,700 target range around a fair value of $1,484.54: expected upside of 9.9%, bear-case downside of 28.9% and reward/risk of 0.34x. The operating record supports owning the business, but at today's price the reward does not cover a stall, and the label depends on whether the current-year multiple compresses as growth slows, which we judge more likely than not but close.

The page's own math sets the triggers. At or below our target low, these scenarios derive BUY; at or above the $1,569.15 Base implied price, they derive SELL. On fundamentals, evidence that the market will keep a current-year multiple near 49.3x on FY27 earnings, such as further enterprise-data growth with operating margin holding, would lift the Base toward a BUY; a quarter in which enterprise data stalls would raise the Bear weight.
